analysis.title: Eq Positioning and Key Levels
key_insights: CTA flows forecast is negligible in a flat tape this week, but over the next month both tails are large: a down tape means $164.42B of selling and an up tape means $120.52B of buying.

GS prime brokerage: global equities were net bought for the first time in a month (+0.3 SDs 1-year) while de-grossing continued for a 3rd straight week, with short covers outpacing long sales 1.8 to 1.

Hedge funds net bought US equities for the first time in 4 weeks (+1.1 SDs 1-year), driven by short covers in Macro Products and to a lesser extent Single Stocks. Macro Products (Index and ETF combined) saw the largest net buying in 3 months and made up 73% of the total.

Friday's session data showed the US net sold (-0.7 SDs 1-year), with short selling outpacing long buying 2.7 to 1. Information Tech was the most net sold US sector (-1.5 SDs), while Consumer Discretionary (+1.5 SDs) and Financials (+1.4 SDs) were the most net bought.

Overall hedge fund book gross leverage rose 1.8 pts to 314.1% (86th percentile 1-year) and net leverage rose 1.8 pts to 73.6% (10th percentile 1-year). Fundamental L/S net leverage is at the 3rd percentile 1-year.
Single Stocks were net sold for a 7th straight week globally, while Macro Products were net bought for a 2nd straight week.

Info Tech remains heavily net sold month to date. This week's net buying through Thursday is about 40% of what hedge funds sold in the previous 3 weeks, and Mag 7 names were collectively net sold in 4 of the past 5 sessions. The desk reads this as little recovery in risk appetite.

Hedge funds unwound risk across US Financials for a second straight week at the fastest pace in more than 6 months, with short covers outpacing long sales 3 to 1. Capital Markets, Financials ETFs and Banks led.

Industrials was the most net sold global sector for a 3rd straight week (5 of the last 6), with the largest % de-grossing in 3 months. EM was the most net sold region, net sold for a 7th straight week.

The GS Equity Systematic L/S performance estimate fell -2.17% from 10/23 to 10/29, the worst weekly drawdown since Dec '23, driven almost entirely by alpha on long side losses. Fundamental L/S rose +1.25%.

Buyback desk flow finished 0.6x vs 2025 YTD ADTV and 0.7x vs 2024 YTD ADTV. About 60% of the S&P 500 is in an open window, with about 82% expected by the end of this week. The desk expects flows to pick up in November, historically its second most active month.

With 60% of S&P 500 companies reported, Q3 2026 EPS growth is on track for 33% y/y, matching Q2 as the strongest quarter in decades outside post-recession recoveries, but ending the pattern of acceleration. GS expects growth of nearly 30% in 2026 slowing to 18% in 2027, excluding non-recurring items.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds remain heavily net sold month to date. Semis & Semi Equip, Software and Tech ETFs were the most net bought subsectors this week, while Tech Hardware and IT Services were most net sold. This is positioning data, not a stated sector view.

Hedge funds de-grossed US Financials for a second straight week at the fastest pace in more than 6 months. Friday saw net buying (+1.4 SDs) led by long buys. This is positioning data, not a stated sector view.
Most net sold global sector for a 3rd straight week, with the largest % de-grossing in 3 months. This is positioning data, not a stated sector view.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 Q3 2026 EPS growth is on track for 33% y/y with 60% of companies reported (estimate based on partial reporting, excluding non-recurring items per the desk's framing). This would match Q2 as the strongest quarter in recent decades outside post-recession recoveries and end the acceleration pattern.
GS expects S&P 500 EPS growth, excluding non-recurring items, of nearly 30% in 2026 (forecast) slowing to 18% in 2027 (forecast).
risk_factors: A down tape over the next month would trigger an estimated $164.42B of CTA selling, larger than the $120.52B of buying in an up tape.
Info Tech hedge fund selling and little recovery in risk appetite amid a busy earnings week and a volatile tech tape.
Slowing S&P 500 EPS growth from about 30% in 2026 to 18% in 2027, and an end to quarterly acceleration in Q3 2026.
vol_and_positioning: CTA flows, next 1 week: flat tape buyers $1.33B ($4.41B out of the US), up tape buyers $26.43B ($5.3B into the US), down tape sellers $40.28B ($19.98B out of the US).
CTA flows, next 1 month: flat tape sellers $11.59B ($16B out of the US), up tape buyers $120.52B ($35.71B into the US), down tape sellers $164.42B ($68.83B out of the US).
SPX key pivot levels: short term 7713, medium term 7544, long term 7082.
A 1x standard deviation market move is 1.62% over 1 week and 3.78% over 1 month.

Hedge fund overall book L/S ratio rose 0.9% to 1.612 (8th percentile 1-year). Gross leverage on Friday was 314.5% (86th percentile 1-year, 97th percentile 5-year) and net leverage 73.4% (9th percentile 1-year, 43rd percentile 5-year).
US Fundamental L/S gross leverage is 216.3% (66th percentile 1-year) and net leverage is 47% (7th percentile 1-year). Beta adjusted fundamental net leverage is 64.8% (3rd percentile 1-year).
